MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

This neuron is negative everywhere in ordinary text and only returns to ~zero on the `<|begin_of_text|>` token, so it acts as a BOS/sequence-start detector; its strongest suppression comes on interior tokens of multi-word proper names or technical compound terms (e.g. "Di **Rosa** Preserve", "DOT **3**", "Brown **Dog** Tick", "time **weighted** average").

L13·N2158unmasked layer
This neuron is essentially an "answer-boundary" detector with inverted sign: it goes strongly negative on the punctuation that closes a question/prompt right before its answer (a "?" followed by newline, or a ":" after a question-like phrase), while its "max" activations are only weakly positive on ordinary mid-sentence tokens (periods, "and", "to", dashes) in continuous prose.

This neuron fires on the punctuation token that closes a caption/attribution/speaker-label unit and opens a new discourse block — sentence-final period-plus-newline, the colon after a dialogue speaker's name, and opening curly quotes introducing a quotation (the same surface forms also appear among its strongest negatives, so it is a structural boundary-punctuation detector whose sign depends on surrounding context rather than a semantic feature).
